item.title: This summer was hot. August shattered global heat records
item.description: Scientists say that August was the hottest month ever recorded globally. In the U.S., summer temperatures also shattered heat records.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: A fossil feather from the age of dinosaurs may explain why only some birds survived
item.description: An extremely well preserved fossil feather could reveal why some birds survived the dinosaur-killing asteroid, and others did not.

item.title: Scientists say August was Earth's hottest month they've measured
item.description: The European climate service Copernicus said the Earth just sweltered through its hottest month on record in August. Scientists said the heat surge is mostly due to human-caused climate change.

item.title: Are we any closer to detecting dark matter?
item.description: NPR's Scott Detrow talks with theoretical astrophysicist Priyamvada Natarajan of Yale University about a strange blip recorded by a dark matter detector in South Dakota and what the fluke could mean.

item.title: 'Her body temperature was 106': How heat is killing Americans in their homes
item.description: Heat kills thousands of people across the U.S. every year. The risk is especially high for the millions of Americans who live in manufactured housing like mobile homes and trailers.

item.title: Biologist Andrew Newhouse on the genetic revival of the American chestnut
item.description: The American chestnut once dominated the Eastern woodlands. NPR's Scott Simon talks to Andrew Newhouse, an environmental biologist, about efforts to bring these trees back from the brink of extinction.

item.description: NPR's Regina Barber and Nate Rott talk about a new way to spot archaeological fakes, how hurricanes may have influenced lizard evolution and the health effects of extreme heat.

item.title: Scientists study how the brain of a fish filters out signals
item.description: The elephantnose fish is native to Africa and a darling of neuroscientists, for its specialized cerebellum-like brain. Scientists have mapped the neurons in a part of the brain that senses electrical signals in detail, and found that how it filters out electrical noise is more complex than they thought.
